q: QPR won the League Cup in 1967, in the first final of that competition staged at Wembley. Which club did they beat 3-2?
hint: The Midlands side were the holders, having won the League Cup the previous season. They led 2-0 at Wembley and still lost.

q: Who was QPR's manager when they finished First Division runners-up in 1975-76?
hint: He arrived at Loftus Road from Chelsea in October 1974 and left for Manchester United in 1977.

q: QPR finished a point behind the champions in the 1975-76 First Division. Which club won the title that season?
hint: Bob Paisley's side took the trophy with 60 points to QPR's 59, winning their final game at Wolves.

q: Which QPR player scored the 81st-minute winner in the 1967 League Cup final?
hint: It was a winger who completed the comeback, not either of the two men who had already pulled the goals back.

q: Stan Bowles became QPR's cult No. 10 of the 1970s. Which club did he join them from in September 1972?
hint: QPR paid £112,000 to the Cumbrian club. Bowles had played for the other three earlier in his travels.

q: Loftus Road, QPR's home since 1917, sits in which part of west London?
hint: The ground is a short walk from the White City site, in the W12 postcode.

q: QPR laid an artificial pitch at Loftus Road in 1981. In which year did they dig it up and go back to grass?
hint: The plastic lasted seven seasons before being removed in the April of that year.

q: Phil Parkes left QPR in February 1979 for £565,000, then a world record fee for a goalkeeper. Which club signed him?
hint: He moved across London and stayed at his new club for eleven years.

q: QPR reached the FA Cup final for the only time in 1982. Which club beat them after a replay?
hint: The north London side were retaining the trophy, having also won a replayed final the year before.

q: Rodney Marsh left QPR in March 1972 for a then club-record fee. Which club did he join?
hint: Malcolm Allison paid £200,000 to take him to Maine Road. He had originally arrived at QPR from Fulham in 1966.

q: QPR finished their 1975-76 league programme top of the table, a point clear of the side who still had a game to play. At which ground was that title-deciding match played ten days later?
hint: The champions' rearranged final fixture was away at Wolves, who needed to win it to stay up.

q: Which division were QPR playing in when they won the 1967 League Cup?
hint: They won that same division's title in the same season, so the cup came with a promotion.

q: QPR's 1981 artificial pitch was the first in British professional football, and three other Football League clubs followed in the 1980s. Which of these was one of them?
hint: Kenilworth Road got its plastic in 1985; Oldham and Preston laid theirs the year after.

q: Which QPR midfielder captained England during the mid-1970s?
hint: He led England in eight of his twelve caps before a persistent back injury cut his international career short.

q: Who scored QPR's equaliser late in extra time of the 1982 FA Cup final at Wembley?
hint: It was a defender who would later win England caps and eventually join the very club that beat him that day.

q: QPR came from behind to win the 1967 League Cup final. What was the score at half-time?
hint: Clive Clark scored twice for the Midlands side inside the first 36 minutes.

q: Which manager took QPR to the 1982 FA Cup final and then to the Second Division title the following season?
hint: He took the job in 1980, installed the plastic pitch, and left for Barcelona in 1984.

q: Don Givens, QPR's leading league scorer in the 1975-76 runners-up season, played international football for which country?
hint: Born in Limerick, the striker won 56 caps between 1969 and 1981.

q: QPR reached the quarter-finals of the 1976-77 UEFA Cup, where they went out on penalties. Which club knocked them out?
hint: QPR won the home leg 3-0, lost the away leg 3-0 in Greece, and then lost the shootout 7-6.

q: QPR were back at Wembley for the 1986 League Cup final, then sponsored as the Milk Cup. Which club beat them 3-0?
hint: It remains the only major trophy won by the Manor Ground club, under manager Maurice Evans.

q: QPR were founder members of the Premier League. Where did they finish in the inaugural 1992-93 season?
hint: They were the highest-placed London club that season, finishing above both Tottenham and Arsenal.

q: The nickname 'the Hoops' comes from the club's shirt. Which two colours are the hoops?
hint: Celtic wear the green version of the same design; the Loftus Road version swaps in a cooler colour.

q: In May 2011 an FA commission fined QPR £875,000 over the registration of one of their midfielders, but imposed no points deduction, so the promotion stood. Which midfielder was at the centre of the case?
hint: The Argentine had joined from Instituto in 2009, and the charges that were dismissed concerned third-party ownership rules.

q: Who scored the 90th-minute goal that won QPR the 2014 Championship play-off final at Wembley?
hint: The veteran striker struck from the edge of the box with almost the last kick of the game.

q: Which manager led QPR to the Championship title and promotion to the Premier League in 2010-11?
hint: He arrived from Crystal Palace in March 2010, and was sacked in January 2012 during the club's first season back in the top flight.

q: QPR led 2-1 away on the final day of 2011-12 before the hosts turned it around in stoppage time. Who scored the goal that had put Rangers in front?
hint: The Scotland forward headed in Armand Traoré's cross just after the hour, with Rangers already down to ten men.

q: QPR lost the 2003 Division Two play-off final at the Millennium Stadium to an extra-time goal. Which club beat them?
hint: Andy Campbell's chip over Chris Day settled it, taking the winners into the second tier for the first time since 1985.

q: QPR were relegated to the third tier at the end of 2000-01, their first drop that low since the 1960s. Which former Rangers midfielder had taken over as manager that February?
hint: He had played for the club in the 1990s before returning to the dugout, and later took them back up as Division Two runners-up in 2004.

q: QPR won the 2014 Championship play-off final at Wembley. Which club did they beat?
hint: The beaten side dominated possession and were managed by Steve McClaren, who called it the cruellest game ever.

q: Which manager was in charge when QPR were relegated from the Premier League at the end of 1995-96?
hint: The former England midfielder took over in late 1994 and left Loftus Road in September 1996.

q: QPR signed Trevor Sinclair in 1993 for a fee that broke his previous club's record for a sale. Which club did he leave?
hint: The £600,000 move took the winger from the Lancashire coast to west London; he went on to join West Ham in 1998.

q: Trevor Sinclair's overhead kick for QPR won the BBC's Goal of the Season in 1997. Which club were the opponents in that FA Cup fourth-round tie?
hint: Rangers won the January tie 3-2 at Loftus Road, and the opponents went up to the Premier League that same season.

q: Which striker scored 24 Premier League goals for QPR in the 1994-95 season?
hint: 'Sir Les' came through non-league football at Hayes before making his name at Loftus Road.

q: QPR sold their leading scorer of the previous season for £6m in the summer of 1995. Which club bought him?
hint: Kevin Keegan's side paid the fee; Ferdinand only moved on to Tottenham two years later.

q: QPR won automatic promotion from Division Two in 2003-04 as runners-up. Which club finished above them as champions?
hint: The Devon club took the title on 90 points, with Bristol City finishing third, a single point behind QPR.

q: QPR played much of the 2014 Championship play-off final with ten men. Which midfielder was sent off in the 60th minute?
hint: He was dismissed for hauling down Johnny Russell as the Derby forward ran through on goal.

q: Harry Redknapp took over as QPR manager in November 2012. Which manager did he replace?
hint: His predecessor had taken just four points from the opening twelve league games of that season.

q: QPR broke their transfer record in January 2013 to sign a defender from Anzhi Makhachkala. Who was he?
hint: The £12.5m fee could not save Rangers, who finished bottom of the table on 25 points that season.

q: Which attacking midfielder was named Championship Player of the Year after scoring 19 league goals in QPR's 2010-11 promotion season?
hint: The Morocco international had signed permanently from Tottenham the previous August.
